points.title: 童年与成长
points.description: 卡夫卡出生于布拉格一个犹太中产阶级家庭。他的父亲赫尔曼·卡夫卡是一位成功的商人，性格专横；母亲朱莉亚则较为温和。卡夫卡从小接受德语教育，生活在多民族、多语言的环境中，这种背景深刻影响了他的世界观。童年时期，卡夫卡经常感受到父亲的权威压力，这种父子关系紧张成为他后来作品中常见的主题。在布拉格的德语中学接受教育，期间展现出对文学和哲学的浓厚兴趣，但也开始感受到社会疏离感和身份认同的困惑。
points.descriptionEn: Kafka was born into a middle-class Jewish family in Prague. His father Hermann Kafka was a successful businessman with an authoritarian personality, while his mother Julie was more gentle. Kafka grew up in a multilingual, multicultural environment that profoundly influenced his worldview. During his childhood, Kafka frequently felt the pressure of his father's authority, a father-son dynamic that became a common theme in his later works. He attended a German-language school in Prague, showing a keen interest in literature and philosophy, but also beginning to experience feelings of social alienation and identity confusion.

points.title: 大学时期
points.description: 卡夫卡进入布拉格查理大学，最初学习化学，后转学法律。大学期间，他结识了马克斯·布罗德等志同道合的朋友，这些友谊对他后来的文学创作产生了重要影响。卡夫卡积极参与学生社团活动，同时开始写作，创作了短篇小说《描述一场斗争》等早期作品。这一时期，他深入研究了克尔凯郭尔、尼采等哲学家的思想，这些哲学思考融入了他的文学创作中。1906年，卡夫卡获得法学博士学位，并在一家保险公司实习，开始了长达14年的保险职业生涯。
points.descriptionEn: Kafka enrolled at Charles University in Prague, initially studying chemistry before switching to law. During his university years, he befriended like-minded individuals including Max Brod, whose friendship would significantly influence his later literary work. Kafka actively participated in student organizations while beginning to write, creating early works such as the short story 'Description of a Struggle.' During this period, he deeply studied philosophers like Kierkegaard and Nietzsche, whose philosophical ideas would be incorporated into his literary creations. In 1906, Kafka received his doctorate in law and began an internship at an insurance company, starting a 14-year career in insurance.

points.title: 职业与创作
points.description: 卡夫卡在工伤保险公司工作，负责处理工伤赔偿案件。这份工作让他接触到社会底层人民的苦难，这些经历成为他创作的重要素材。同时，他继续文学创作，完成了《变形记》《在流放地》《乡村医生》等重要作品。这一时期，卡夫卡与菲利斯·鲍尔订婚又解除婚约，这种情感上的不稳定状态反映在他的作品中。他与马克斯·布罗德等朋友定期聚会，讨论文学和哲学，形成了布拉格文学圈。卡夫卡的作品开始在小圈子里流传，但尚未获得广泛认可。他的创作风格逐渐成熟，以荒诞、异化和官僚制度批判为主题。
points.descriptionEn: Kafka worked at the Worker's Accident Insurance Institute, handling compensation cases for industrial injuries. This job exposed him to the suffering of working-class people, experiences that became important material for his writing. Simultaneously, he continued his literary work, completing major pieces such as 'The Metamorphosis,' 'In the Penal Colony,' and 'A Country Doctor.' During this period, Kafka became engaged to and then broke off his engagement with Felice Bauer, emotional instability that reflected in his works. He regularly met with friends including Max Brod to discuss literature and philosophy, forming a Prague literary circle. Kafka's works began to circulate in small circles but had not yet gained wide recognition. His writing style gradually matured, focusing on themes of absurdity, alienation, and critique of bureaucracy.

points.title: 疾病与创作高峰
points.description: 1917年，卡夫卡被诊断出患有肺结核，这成为他生命的重要转折点。他多次前往疗养院治疗，包括施皮茨的疗养院。尽管健康状况恶化，卡夫卡进入了创作高峰期，完成了《审判》《美国》《城堡》等重要长篇小说的初稿。这一时期，他与米莲娜·耶申斯卡有过一段短暂而深刻的恋情，但最终因健康原因而分离。卡夫卡对犹太文化的兴趣也日益浓厚，开始研究犹太教哈西德派传统。他的作品风格更加成熟，对官僚制度、异化感和存在困境的探索更加深入。1922年，卡夫卡辞去保险公司工作，专注于写作。
points.descriptionEn: In 1917, Kafka was diagnosed with tuberculosis, a turning point in his life. He sought treatment at various sanatoriums, including one in Spitz. Despite his deteriorating health, Kafka entered a period of intense creativity, completing first drafts of major novels including 'The Trial,' 'The Man Who Disappeared' (Amerika), and 'The Castle.' During this time, he had a brief but profound relationship with Milena Jesenská, which ultimately ended due to his health condition. Kafka's interest in Jewish culture also grew, and he began studying Hasidic traditions. His writing style matured further, with deeper exploration of themes of bureaucracy, alienation, and existential dilemmas. In 1922, Kafka resigned from his insurance job to focus on writing.

points.title: 最后岁月
points.description: 卡夫卡的健康状况持续恶化，他前往维也纳附近的基尔林疗养院接受治疗。在生命的最后阶段，他继续写作，完成了短篇小说《饥饿艺术家》等作品，并开始创作《地洞》等未完成作品。卡夫卡指示好友马克斯·布罗德在他死后销毁所有未发表的手稿，但布罗德违背了他的遗愿，整理并出版了他的作品，使卡夫卡在死后获得了广泛的认可和声誉。1924年6月3日，卡夫卡在基尔林疗养院去世，年仅40岁。他的作品在20世纪中期开始产生深远影响，成为现代主义文学的重要代表，对存在主义文学和荒诞派戏剧产生了重要影响。
points.descriptionEn: Kafka's health continued to deteriorate, and he sought treatment at a sanatorium in Kierling near Vienna. In his final months, he continued writing, completing works such as 'A Hunger Artist' and beginning unfinished pieces like 'The Burrow.' Kafka instructed his friend Max Brod to destroy all his unpublished manuscripts after his death, but Brod disregarded these wishes, editing and publishing his works, which led to Kafka's posthumous recognition and reputation. On June 3, 1924, Kafka died in the Kierling sanatorium at the age of 40. His works began to have profound influence in the mid-20th century, becoming an important representative of modernist literature and significantly influencing existentialist literature and the Theater of the Absurd.

supporter.zh: 卡夫卡被誉为现代主义文学的先驱，他的作品深刻揭示了现代人的异化处境和存在困境。支持者认为，卡夫卡通过荒诞的叙事手法，精准捕捉了现代社会中个体与官僚制度、家庭和社会的疏离感。他的作品超越了时代限制，成为20世纪人类精神困境的象征。卡夫卡对语言和形式的创新，以及对人类处境的深刻洞察，使他成为世界文学史上最具影响力的作家之一。他的作品不仅具有文学价值，更成为理解现代社会和人类存在的重要哲学文本。
supporter.en: Kafka is hailed as a pioneer of modernist literature, whose works profoundly reveal the alienation and existential predicament of modern humans. Supporters argue that through absurd narrative techniques, Kafka accurately captured the sense of alienation between individuals and bureaucratic systems, families, and society. His works transcended temporal limitations, becoming symbols of the spiritual predicament of humanity in the 20th century. Kafka's innovations in language and form, combined with his profound insights into the human condition, make him one of the most influential writers in literary history. His works possess not only literary value but also serve as important philosophical texts for understanding modern society and human existence.

critic.zh: 批评者认为卡夫卡的作品过于悲观和绝望，缺乏积极的人文关怀。他们指出，卡夫卡笔下的人物往往被动接受命运，缺乏反抗精神，这种消极态度可能强化了现代人的无力感。此外，一些批评者认为卡夫卡的作品过于个人化，难以引起广泛共鸣，其晦涩难懂的叙事风格也限制了读者群体。还有人质疑卡夫卡对犹太身份的矛盾态度，认为这种矛盾反映了他文化归属的混乱。批评者认为，卡夫卡的文学成就虽然不可否认，但其作品中的消极主义和对人类处境的悲观描绘可能对读者产生负面影响。
critic.en: Critics argue that Kafka's works are excessively pessimistic and despairing, lacking positive humanistic concern. They point out that characters in Kafka's narratives often passively accept their fate without resistance, and this消极 attitude may reinforce the sense of powerlessness in modern individuals. Additionally, some critics believe Kafka's works are overly personal, making it difficult to achieve broad resonance, and his obscure narrative style limits his readership. Others question Kafka's ambivalent attitude toward his Jewish identity, suggesting this reflects confusion about his cultural belonging. Critics acknowledge Kafka's undeniable literary achievements but argue that the pessimism and bleak portrayal of the human condition in his works may have negative effects on readers.

objective.zh: 从历史与流行文化视角看，卡夫卡已成为一个文化符号，代表着现代人的异化处境和存在困境。他的名字'卡夫卡式'已成为形容词，用来描述荒诞、官僚化的处境。在学术界，卡夫卡的作品被从多种角度解读，包括马克思主义、精神分析、后结构主义等。卡夫卡的影响超越了文学领域，延伸到电影、戏剧、艺术等多个文化领域。他的作品被翻译成多种语言，在全球范围内广泛传播。卡夫卡生前默默无闻，死后却成为世界文学巨匠，这一反差本身已成为文学史上的传奇。他的作品不仅反映了特定历史时期的社会现实，更触及了人类普遍的生存困境，使其成为跨越时空的文化现象。
objective.en: From a historical and popular culture perspective, Kafka has become a cultural symbol representing the alienation and existential predicament of modern humans. His name 'Kafkaesque' has become an adjective used to describe absurd and bureaucratic situations. In academia, Kafka's works have been interpreted from various perspectives, including Marxism, psychoanalysis, and poststructuralism. Kafka's influence extends beyond literature into film, theater, art, and other cultural domains. His works have been translated into numerous languages and widely disseminated globally. Kafka's posthumous fame contrasts with his obscurity during his lifetime, making this contrast itself a legend in literary history. His works not only reflect the social realities of a specific historical period but also address universal human existential dilemmas, making them a transhistorical and transcultural phenomenon.

self.zh: 一本书必须是像一把冰冷的铁锥，砸进我们脑子的冰冷的铁锥。
self.en: A book must be the axe for the frozen sea within us.

others.zh: 卡夫卡是我们这个时代最伟大的作家之一，他的作品揭示了人类存在的根本困境。
others.en: Kafka is one of the greatest writers of our time, his works reveal the fundamental predicament of human existence.
